summary: Shows conditionals on a registered result's status (is failed, succeeded, skipped, changed) with ignore_errors, and using the implicit _task variable in loops to check the previous iteration's result or accumulated loop_result, with default for the first iteration.
questions: How do I run a task only if a previous task failed?
How do I check if a registered task changed something?
How do I stop a loop after a previous iteration fails?
What is the _task variable in loops?
Is it success or succeeded in when conditions?

answer_card.title: Testing task status and previous loop iterations
answer_card.answer_md:
```yaml
- ansible.builtin.command: /bin/false
  register: result
  ignore_errors: true
- ansible.builtin.command: /bin/something
  when: result is failed     # or succeeded / skipped / changed
```

(`success`/`fail` still work but `succeeded`/`failed` are preferred.)

In loops, `_task` gives the previous iteration's result; provide a default for the first item:

```yaml
loop: [initialize, validate, deploy]
when: _task.result | default({}) is not failed and _task.result | default({}) is not skipped
```

All accumulated results: `when: (_task.loop_result.results | default([]) | length) < 2`.
